competencies.text: Explain unique landforms, climate, and life forms of the Philippines.

days.title: Landforms, Climate & Life
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe the unique landforms, climate types, and biodiversity of the Philippines, and explain how they are connected.

🏔️ Unique Landforms of the Philippines

The Philippines has a wide variety of landforms shaped by its tectonic history and tropical climate:

LandformDescriptionExample
VolcanoesMountains formed by magma rising through subduction zonesMayon, Taal, Pinatubo, Apo, Kanlaon
Mountain rangesChains of mountains formed by uplift and faultingCordillera, Sierra Madre, Kitanglad
Rolling hillsRounded hills formed by weatheringChocolate Hills (Bohol), Batanes hills
Karst landscapesLimestone formations with caves and underground riversPuerto Princesa Underground River, Sagada caves
Rice terracesHuman-made stepped slopes for farmingBanaue Rice Terraces
Coastal landformsBeaches, coral reefs, mangroves, lagoonsBoracay, Tubbataha Reefs, Palawan
Valleys & plainsLow-lying areas for agricultureCentral Luzon Plain, Cagayan Valley

🌦️ Climate Types of the Philippines

The Philippines has a tropical maritime climate, influenced by:

  • Its location near the equator
  • Surrounding warm ocean waters
  • Monsoon winds (Amihan and Habagat)
  • Typhoons that pass through the region

The four climate types (PAGASA classification based on rainfall distribution):

TypeDescriptionRegions
Type ITwo distinct seasons: dry (Nov–Apr) and wet (May–Oct)Ilocos, Central Luzon, parts of Mindanao
Type IINo dry season — rainfall distributed throughout the yearBicol, Eastern Visayas, Eastern Mindanao
Type IIISeasons not very pronounced — relatively dry (Dec–Feb)Cagayan, Isabela, Nueva Vizcaya
Type IVRainfall more or less evenly distributedBatanes, Aurora, parts of Mindoro

💨 Monsoon Winds

WindDirectionSeasonEffect
Amihan (NE monsoon)From northeastNovember–FebruaryCool, dry season
Habagat (SW monsoon)From southwestJune–OctoberWet season with rains

🌪️ Typhoon Belt

The Philippines is in the typhoon belt — about 20 tropical cyclones enter Philippine waters each year, with about 8–9 making landfall. This is due to:

  • Warm ocean temperatures (at least 26.5°C)
  • Location in the western Pacific
  • Coriolis effect away from the equator

🌱 Biodiversity of the Philippines

The Philippines is one of 17 megadiverse countries — together they contain 70% of the world's biodiversity.

GroupPH Significance
PlantsOver 10,000 species; ~65% are endemic (found only in PH)
BirdsOver 700 species; ~240 endemic — like the Philippine Eagle
MammalsOver 200 species; ~100 endemic — like the Tamaraw, Visayan Warty Pig
Reptiles & amphibiansOver 400 species; ~65% endemic
Marine lifePart of the Coral Triangle — 2,500+ fish species, 500+ coral species

🦅 Iconic Species of the Philippines

  • Philippine Eagle — one of the largest eagles in the world; critically endangered
  • Tamaraw — small buffalo found only in Mindoro
  • Visayan Warty Pig — critically endangered
  • Palawan Peacock-Pheasant — endemic to Palawan
  • Philippine Tarsier — one of the smallest primates
  • Whale sharks (Butanding) — spotted in Donsol, Sorsogon

🌏 Why Biodiversity Matters

Biodiversity provides:

  • Food security — fisheries, agriculture, forest products
  • Medicine — many drugs derive from natural sources
  • Ecosystem services — clean water, air, fertile soil
  • Cultural value — Indigenous peoples depend on forests and reefs
  • Climate regulation — forests and oceans absorb CO₂

⚠️ Threats to Philippine Biodiversity

  • Deforestation (illegal logging, mining, land conversion)
  • Overfishing and destructive fishing (dynamite, cyanide)
  • Habitat loss from urbanization
  • Climate change
  • Wildlife trafficking
  • Pollution

📌 Quick Check

  • How many climate types does PAGASA classify in the Philippines? (Answer: four — Types I–IV)
  • What are the two monsoon winds? (Answer: Amihan from NE, Habagat from SW)
  • What percentage of Philippine plants are endemic? (Answer: about 65%)

days.title: Match Game — Philippine Landforms
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each Philippine landform, climate concept, or species to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Rounded hills in Bohol formed by weathering of limestone
Human-made stepped slopes in the Cordillera for farming
Karst landscape with a cave and river in Palawan
Cool, dry wind from the northeast — November to February
Warm, wet wind from the southwest — June to October
Zone where ~20 tropical cyclones pass each year over the Philippines
One of the largest eagles in the world — critically endangered
Marine region including the Philippines with 2,500+ fish species

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Biodiversity Hotspots
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🌾 A farmer in Cagayan Valley (Climate Type III) asks when the driest months usually are. What should you tell them?

choices.label: A) December to February — Type III has a relatively dry season during these months
C) There is no dry season
D) Rainfall is distributed evenly all year

scenario.text: 🦅 A birdwatcher wants to see the Philippine Eagle in the wild. Where should they go?

choices.label: A) The remaining forests of Mindanao, Luzon, and Samar — its natural habitat
C) The Chocolate Hills in Bohol
D) The rice terraces of Banaue

scenario.text: 🌊 A marine biologist studies the Coral Triangle. Why is the Philippines a critical part of this region?

choices.label: A) The Philippines lies at the heart of the Coral Triangle — with over 500 coral species and 2,500 fish species
B) The Philippines has the largest ocean
C) The Philippines is outside the Coral Triangle
D) The Coral Triangle is a man-made reserve

scenario.text: 🌪️ A typhoon is expected to make landfall in Eastern Visayas in November. Which type of climate does this region have?

choices.label: A) Type II — no dry season, rainfall throughout the year, high typhoon exposure
B) Type I — two distinct seasons
C) Type III — short dry season
D) Type IV — evenly distributed rainfall

scenario.text: 🐒 A Visayan Warty Pig is critically endangered. What is the MAIN threat to its survival?

choices.label: A) Habitat loss from deforestation and hunting
B) Too many pigs in the forest

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Biodiversity Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Biodiversity Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: How many climate types does PAGASA classify in the Philippines?
Which monsoon wind brings cool, dry weather from November to February?
How many tropical cyclones typically enter Philippine waters each year?

choices.label: A) A marine region including the Philippines with 2,500+ fish species and 500+ coral species
B) A political alliance of three countries
C) A type of coral reef

escape.text: What percentage of Philippine plants are endemic (found only in the Philippines)?
Which of the following is the MOST serious threat to Philippine biodiversity?

choices.label: A) Habitat loss from deforestation, mining, and land conversion
